newsitem.title: UK: Canada's AMT to rejuvenate old metal resources.
newsitem.headline: Canada's AMT to rejuvenate old metal resources.

text.p: Applied Mine Technologies Inc (AMT) of Canada, which is currently seeking a listing on the Toronto Stock Exchange, aims to bring to life old metal resources previously deemed uneconomic.
At a presentation here AMT President and Chief Executive Officer Bob Baldock said the company will use innovative technology, including bioleaching, on metallurgically complex projects.
The intention is to negotiate agreements, take projects through to pre-feasability, set up potential financing, and then offer the package to a major mining company.

AMT has targetted the Old Nick nickel/cobalt project in British Colombia as its initial venture. This was discovered in 1966 by Newmont Mining, and is estimated to contain a potential 100 million tonne resource.

AMT has options to acquire up to a 50 percent equity interest in the project. It is currently 50 percent owned by Gold City Mining Corporation, 25 percent by Phoenix Gold Resources, and 25 percent by Orion International Minerals Corporation.
Initial estimates show that the project could produce 6,500 tonnes a year of nickel and 325 tonnes annually of cobalt.
Operating costs for nickel production will be $1.45/lb, against current prices around $3.35/lb, and assuming a by-product cobalt value of $12/lb.
"From present indications there is a substantial orebody there...There are no reasons why this cannot be permitted," Baldock said.
AMT will look to have around three or four projects on the blocks, and intends initially to remain in North America.
""We are not tempted to go somewhere else...we have enough projects in North America," Baldock said.
Its other projects are Domin/Welbar gold in British Colombia and Valentine gold on Vancouver Island.
